new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for Katla; this is the first sourced statement: tone and stress both exist (after Stevenson 1956-57), placement not stated. WARNING: three other archive.org snippets that earlier turned up for this item are NOT from the Katla chapter and must not be attributed to Katla: 'Stress is normally on the first syllable of disyllabic words..' (Bongo-Bagirmi chapter; its continuation cites 'BAGIRMI kala, snake'), 'Stress.. seems to fall on the first syllable of a word Stem. The Noun Class Suffix is never stressed' (Moru-Mangbetu chapter; continuation cites the MANGBUTU-EFE Group), and '2b. Stress is often on the antepenultimate syllable, e.g. tumpul…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Katla has both tone and stress according to Stevenson's survey material; Tucker & Bryan give lexical tone doublets but state no rule for where stress falls, and their examples are not marked for tone or stress.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the section says only that stress exists, with no placement, so nothing to except from
new_statements.identity_note: Tucker & Bryan's chapter 'The Katla Group' covers Katla and Tima together, but its head states 'All examples are from KATLA unless otherwise stated', and sec. 2 names no Tima data, so the tone-and-stress statement is about Katla proper (Stevenson's 1956-57 survey material plus personal communication from Stevenson).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid records katl1237 (Katla) and julu1237 (Julud), and reference records 24688, 325512, 588880, 575578, 588881.
sources.note: katl1237 Glottolog's most extensive description = Meinhof 1916-17 only; julu1237 Glottolog's most extensive descriptions = Nüsslein 2020 (grammar sketch), Nüsslein 2019 (Erfurt PhD), Nüsslein 2018 'Number marking in Julut' (NMLS New Insights 281-295), Knoblecher 1849. Glottolog note: Julud mutually intelligible with Katla-Kulharong but not with Katla-Cakom (p.c. Hellwig 2007).
